title: Constitutional Architecture Statement v1.0 — A Definitive Reference for the Status and Relationship of Governance Instruments under the Constitution of the Semantic Economy
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
The canonical status reference for the Semantic Economy governance architecture. The Statement is definitive as a record of current relationships but is non-amending and non-binding by itself: it cannot enact the Constitution, ratify companions, or create new authority.

It organizes governance objects into four tiers—enacted constitutional spine, operative frameworks binding by reference, proposed companion instruments requiring Class II recognition, and a proposed Class III constitutional amendment—while placing other standing instruments outside the core. It also defines enacted, foundational, proposed, provisional, non-authoritative, superseded, and withdrawn states and specifies the ratification path for each class.

wiki_article:
The **Constitutional Architecture Statement v1.0** answers a status question: which Semantic Economy documents bind, which guide, which are proposed, and which merely route?

The Statement is a canonical reference on architecture, but it is not itself an amendment or source of binding authority.

Four tiers are defined.
